name: HIH6130 humidity & temperature sensor
description: Honeywell HumidIcon HIH6130 digital relative humidity (0–100 %, ±4 %RH) and temperature (-25 to 85 °C operating, ±1 °C) sensor with 14-bit I2C output at address 0x27. Runs on 2.3–5.5 V. Sold as: SparkFun Humidity and Temperature Sensor Breakout - HIH6130 (SEN-11295; 6-pin header SDA, SCL, AL_L, AL_H, VDD, GND, with 2.2 kΩ I2C pull-ups to VDD).
eli5: Tells your board how damp the air is and how warm it is.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (2.2 kΩ pull-up to VDD on the board)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (2.2 kΩ pull-up to VDD on the board)

pins.name: AL_L
pins.description: Low alarm output (configured in command mode); not needed for basic use

pins.name: AL_H
pins.description: High alarm output (configured in command mode); not needed for basic use

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply, 2.3–5.5 V straight to the chip (calibrated at 3.3 V); use your board's logic voltage

supplierQuery: HIH6130 humidity temperature sensor breakout I2C
buildNotes: Measurement Request: write the address with no data bytes (i2c.writeto(0x27, b"")), wait at least 37 ms (typically 36.65 ms), then read 4 bytes.
Byte 0 bits 7:6 are status: 00 = new data, 01 = stale (read again a little later), 11 = diagnostic fault. Humidity is the low 14 bits of bytes 0–1; temperature is bytes 2–3 shifted right by 2.
RH = count × 100 / 16383 %, T = count × 165 / 16383 − 40 °C (Honeywell TN, 2^14 − 1 counts full scale).
Wait 60 ms after power-up before the first measurement.
VDD feeds the chip and the 2.2 kΩ pull-ups directly, so power it from 3.3 V on an ESP32 or Pico.
Keep it away from the regulator and the microcontroller, which warm the air nearby; it is calibrated at 3.3 V.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from hih6130 import HIH6130

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = HIH6130(i2c)
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.1fC H=%.0f%%' % (t, h))
    time.sleep(1)
